cases.evidence: Boundary after the name cut off the finite verb, so the next piece 'XDR-TB' was rendered as if appositive to the name (omitted 'discovered').
cases.proposed_rule: Demote any candidate that would leave the left piece as a very short NP (1–2 content words) ending in a title/name or pronoun; prefer boundaries that include the immediately following finite verb.

example_pair.input: Dr. Tony Moll discovered the Extremely Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB) in the South African region KwaZulu-Natal.
example_pair.output: Dr. Tony Moll discovered <SEG:1> the Extremely Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB) <SEG:2> in the South African region KwaZulu-Natal.

cases.evidence: Cut before the appositive/locative cluster caused the ethnonym to be attached with the wrong scope (which country it names).
cases.proposed_rule: Demote boundaries that end on an ethnonym/demonym when a comma-appositive or a locative PP (e.g. starting with 'in') appears within the next ~4 tokens; keep the appositive/locative with that ethnonym.

example_pair.input: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.
example_pair.output: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.<SEG:1>

cases.evidence: Boundary after the verb separated the verb from its immediately following PP complement ('from the heart...'), forcing a guess about the predicate's object/path.
cases.proposed_rule: Demote boundaries that end immediately after a finite verb when the next token begins a prepositional complement (from/to/in/into/through/by/at/with); keep verb+PP together.

example_pair.input: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.
example_pair.output: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins.<SEG:1> The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

cases.evidence: Cut before the reporting clause's main verb ('suspect') left a pronoun-only piece and so the following fragment was rendered incorrectly/contradicted the whole sentence.
cases.proposed_rule: Demote any candidate that would leave the left piece as a single pronoun or auxiliary (they/he/she/we/it) when the next token is a lexical verb or main predicate; prefer including the verb in the same piece.

example_pair.input: Police said they suspect an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant of responsibility for the attack.
example_pair.output: Police said they suspect <SEG:1> an alleged Daesh (ISIL) militant of responsibility for the attack.

summary: The prompt systematically over-trusts boundaries that leave extremely short left pieces (single names, pronouns, or 1–2 token NPs) or that cut at commas before appositives/locative PPs. Empirical over-trust of comma positions (feature '뒤 구두점 ","') and short left chunks is causing many 'head not yet arrived' and 'modifier scope' failures; prefer boundaries that keep a verb with its complements and keep ethnonym+appositive/locative clusters together by demoting those candidates' confidence.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
